changes.text: The seismic-coefficient section applies five Newmark permanent-displacement formulations: three rigid-block models, two flexible-block models and, among the latter, the BM branch selected by the tectonic control of the project. This section reproduces the published form of each formulation, including both BM branches, and states the rule that defines the active configuration. The rigid-block formulations relate the displacement to measures of the base excitation, whereas the flexible-block formulations additionally incorporate the dynamic response of the sliding mass through its fundamental period Ts and the spectral acceleration evaluated at a period proportional to Ts.

changes.text: The Newmark permanent displacement Dn quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The Dn(ky) curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration ky to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with an ensemble set of AM88 (Ambraseys & Menu, 1988), JB07 (Jibson, 2007), SR08 (Saygili & Rathje, 2008), BT07 (Bray & Travasarou, 2007), and BM19 (Bray, Macedo, & Travasauro, 2018), with reference magnitudes Mw = 5.5 and Mw = 6.5 assigned according to the seismic demand and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles q=1-pe. The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient kh is in turn derived from the allowable permanent displacement Da of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, Pseudostatic Coefficient for Use in Simplified Seismic Slope Stability Evaluation, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018); the coefficients are reported at four relative displacement limits, Da/Hs = 0.1, 0.4, 1.0, 2.5%, and the tables in Section 10.3 and 11Appendix E report, for the demands and scenarios analyzed, the coefficient at each limit, expressed as a percentage of the PGA.

changes.text: For each model and realization, the computed Dn(ky) relation is projected onto a non-increasing curve and inverted in the (lnDn,lnky) plane to solve the criterion of Eq. 1014; when Da falls outside the calculated range, the relation is extrapolated in that plane from the two points at the corresponding end, with the single exception of the AM88 limit treated in 11Appendix E. The inversion is performed first for each model within each realization.
